# Implemented a fullscreen drawing-based inspiration flow for Thumbfast

Rollout context: The user asked to replace the Excalidraw-style inspiration path with a custom Thumbfast drawing editor that creates editable drawing inspirations, saves them as normal inspirations with durable preview images, restores the editable scene later, and integrates with existing YouTube/upload inspiration flows, selector/list/detail views, and thumbnail generation.

## Task 1: Build and integrate the drawing inspiration experience

Outcome: partial

Preference signals:
- The user explicitly said: "Do not use Excalidraw" and "Do not ship a modal-only editor" -> future implementations should default to a custom fullscreen editor, not a wrapper or dialog-based shortcut.
- The user asked for a dedicated fullscreen page with "Draw inspiration" / "Create from drawing" entry points -> future work should expose drawing as a first-class create/edit route, not a hidden side panel.
- The user required drawings to be editable after save and reopen -> future implementations should persist structured scene data, not just a flattened image.
- The user required drawing inspirations to appear in the normal inspiration grid/list and be selectable for thumbnail generation -> future integrations should treat drawings as a subtype of inspiration, not a separate silo.

Key steps:
- Inspected the existing inspiration flow, Convex schema/actions, generation prompt path, and selector/detail surfaces before editing.
- Added `drawingMetadata` to the `inspirations` table and surfaced a derived `isDrawing` flag in the query/DTO layer instead of adding a separate schema field for the UI state.
- Added new Convex mutations for creating and updating drawing-backed inspirations, reusing the existing durable inspiration image path for the rendered preview.
- Built a custom drawing feature module with:
  - a structured document/object model,
  - SVG-based interaction rendering,
  - canvas-based preview export,
  - object types for text, arrows, rectangles, ellipses, pencil strokes, image insertion, and person placeholders,
  - starter templates,
  - undo/redo, duplicate, copy/paste, delete, Escape handling, and unsaved-change protection.
- Wired fullscreen create/edit entry points into existing inspiration routes using query-state driven navigation (`?mode=drawing`) instead of adding new route-tree churn.
- Added drawing badges and edit actions to the inspiration list, detail page, detail dialog, and multi-selector.
- Updated `convex/editor.ts` so drawing inspirations are treated as loose sketches that should become polished realistic thumbnails, with permissive redesign guidance.

Failures and how to do differently:
- A naïve route addition using new `/draw` files conflicted with TanStack route generation, so the implementation pivoted to query-based fullscreen modes on existing routes (`/inspirations/new?mode=drawing` and `/$inspirationId?mode=drawing`).
- `tsc` still reports a pre-existing repo baseline error in `src/components/ai-elements/message.tsx:333` from the Streamdown/Shiki type mismatch; that is unrelated to the drawing feature.
- Early implementation passes surfaced style/type issues in the new drawing modules (array-type linting, normalization typing, promise async warnings); those were fixed before the final lint pass.

Reusable knowledge:
- `drawingMetadata` is the durable source of truth for drawing-backed inspirations; deriving `isDrawing` from it is enough for badges and avoids schema churn.
- The generation prompt branch for drawings lives in `convex/editor.ts` inside `getInspirationGenerationDescription(inspiration)`.
- Existing inspiration storage already persists durable preview images, so the drawing feature can save a rendered PNG through the same image path and store the editable scene separately.
- Query-based fullscreen modes are a practical way to add editor entry points in this repo when route generation is awkward.

- `src/features/drawing/drawing-inspiration-page.tsx` — save/load wrapper that renders preview, uploads it, and persists the drawing document.

item.aggregated_output: --- name: make-interfaces-feel-better description: Design engineering principles for making interfaces feel polished. Use when building UI components, reviewing frontend code, implementing animations, hover states, shadows, borders, typography, micro-interactions, enter/exit animations, or any visual detail work. Triggers on UI polish, design details, "make it feel better", "feels off", stagger animations, border radius, optical alignment, font smoothing, tabular numbers, image outlines, box shadows. --- # Details that make interfaces feel better Great interfaces rarely come from a single thing. It's usually a collection of small details that compound into a great experience. Apply these principles when building or reviewing UI code. ## Quick Reference | Category | When to Use | | --- | --- | | [Typography](typography.md) | Text wrapping, font smoothing, tabular numbers | | [Surfaces](surfaces.md) | Border radius, optical alignment, shadows, image outlines, hit areas | | [Animations](animations.md) | Interruptible animations, enter/exit transitions, icon animations, scale on press | | [Performance](performance.md) | Transition specificity, `will-change` usage | ## Core Principles ### 1. Concentric Border Radius Outer radius = inner radius + padding. Mismatched radii on nested elements is the most common thing that makes interfaces feel off. ### 2. Optical Over Geometric Alignment When geometric centering looks off, align optically. Buttons with icons, play triangles, and asymmetric icons all need manual adjustment. ### 3. Shadows Over Borders Layer multiple transparent `box-shadow` values for natural depth. Shadows adapt to any background; solid borders don't. ### 4. Interruptible Animations Use CSS transitions for interactive state changes — they can be interrupted mid-animation. Reserve keyframes for staged sequences that run once. ### 5. Split and Stagger Enter Animations Don't animate a single container. Break content into semantic chunks and stagger each with ~100ms delay. ### 6. Subtle Exit Animations Use a small fixed `translateY` instead of full height. Exits should be softer than enters. ### 7. Contextual Icon Animations Animate icons with `opacity`, `scale`, and `blur` instead of toggling visibility. Use exactly these values: scale from `0.25` to `1`, opacity from `0` to `1`, blur from `4px` to `0px`. If the project has `motion` or `framer-motion` in `package.json`, use `transition: { type: "spring", duration: 0.3, bounce: 0 }` — bounce must always be `0`. If no motion library is installed, keep both icons in the DOM (one absolute-positioned) and cross-fade with CSS transitions using `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` — this gives both enter and exit animations without any dependency. ### 8. Font Smoothing Apply `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` to the root layout on macOS for crisper text. ### 9. Tabular Numbers Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for any dynamically updating numbers to prevent layout shift. ### 10. Text Wrapping Use `text-wrap: balance` on headings. Use `text-wrap: pretty` for body text to avoid orphans. ### 11. Image Outlines Add a subtle `1px` outline with low opacity to images for consistent depth. The color must be pure black in light mode (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)`) and pure white in dark mode (`rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1)`) — never a near-black like slate, zinc, or any tinted neutral. A tinted outline picks up the surface color underneath it and reads as dirt on the image edge. ### 12. Scale on Press A subtle `scale(0.96)` on click gives buttons tactile feedback. Always use `0.96`. Never use a value smaller than `0.95` — anything below feels exaggerated. Add a `static` prop to disable it when motion would be distracting. ### 13. Skip Animation on Page Load Use `initial={false}` on `AnimatePresence` to prevent enter animations on first render. Verify it doesn't break intentional entrance animations. ### 14. Never Use `transition: all` Always specify exact properties: `transition-property: scale, opacity`. Tailwind's `transition-transform` covers `transform, translate, scale, rotate`. ### 15. Use `will-change` Sparingly Only for `transform`, `opacity`, `filter` — properties the GPU can composite. Never use `will-change: all`. Only add when you notice first-frame stutter. ### 16. Minimum Hit Area Interactive elements need at least 40×40px hit area. Extend with a pseudo-element if the visible element is smaller. Never let hit areas of two elements overlap. ## Common Mistakes | Mistake | Fix | | --- | --- | | Same border radius on parent and child | Calculate `outerRadius = innerRadius + padding` | | Icons look off-center | Adjust optically with padding or fix SVG directly | | Hard borders between sections | Use layered `box-shadow` with transparency | | Jarring enter/exit animations | Split, stagger, and keep exits subtle | | Numbers cause layout shift | Apply `tabular-nums` | | Heavy text on macOS | Apply `antialiased` to root | | Animation plays on page load | Add `initial={false}` to `AnimatePresence` | | `transition: all` on elements | Specify exact properties | | First-frame animation stutter | Add `will-change: transform` (sparingly) | | Tiny hit areas on small controls | Extend with pseudo-element to 40×40px | ## Review Output Format Always present changes as a markdown table with **Before** and **After** columns. Include every change you made — not just a subset. Never list findings as separate "Before:" / "After:" lines outside of a table. Group changes by principle using a heading above each table, and keep each row focused on a single diff so the reader can scan the whole list quickly. ### Example #### Concentric border radius | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `rounded-xl` on card + `rounded-xl` on inner button (`p-2`) | `rounded-2xl` on card (`12 + 8`), `rounded-lg` on inner button | | `border-radius: 16px` on both nested surfaces | Outer `24px`, inner `16px` with `8px` padding | #### Tabular numbers | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `{count}` on animated counter | `{count}` | | Default numerals on timer | Added `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` to root | #### Scale on press | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `

    rating: v.optional(v.number()),

    .index("by_legacy", ["legacyId"])
    .index("by_reply_created", ["reply", "createdAt"])

  signupCreditGrants: defineTable({

    .index("by_organization", ["organizationId"])
    .index("by_legacy", ["legacyId"]),

  trialRedemptions: defineTable({
    organizationId: v.string(),

    fingerprint: v.optional(v.string()),

    stripeCustomerId: v.optional(v.string()),

    .index("by_user", ["userId"])
    .index("by_fingerprint", ["fingerprint"])
    .index("by_organization", ["organizationId"])
    .index("by_stripe_subscription", ["stripeSubscriptionId"])

const geminiFeatureAccessRef = makeFunctionReference<
  "query",
  {
    orgId: string;
    creditCost: number;
    featureName: string;
  },
  { shouldDeductCredits: boolean; encryptedGeminiKey?: string }
>("inspiration:geminiFeatureAccess");

type ActionCtx = {
  runQuery: (fn: any, args: any) => Promise<any>;
  runMutation: (fn: any, args: any) => Promise<any>;
};

async function validateCreditForFeature(
  ctx: ActionCtx,
  args: {
    orgId: string;
    creditCost: number;
    featureName: string;
  },
) {
  return ctx.runQuery(geminiFeatureAccessRef, args);
}

async function getGeminiApiKeyIfNeeded(
  shouldDeductCredits: boolean,
  encryptedGeminiKey?: string,
) {
  if (shouldDeductCredits) return undefined;
  return encryptedGeminiKey ? decryptApiKey(encryptedGeminiKey) : undefined;
}

async function logGeminiUsageIfCustomKey(
  ctx: ActionCtx,
  orgId: string,
  customApiKey: string | undefined,
  model?: string,
) {
  if (!customApiKey) return;
  await ctx.runMutation((internal as any).userImages.logCustomGeminiUsage, {
    orgId,
    model,
  });
}

type AnonymizationOptions = {
  subject: boolean;
  text: boolean;
  logos: boolean;
};

function getAnonymizationOptions(args: {
  anonymize?: boolean;
  anonymizeSubject?: boolean;
  anonymizeText?: boolean;
  anonymizeLogos?: boolean;
}): AnonymizationOptions {
  return {
    subject: args.anonymizeSubject ?? args.anonymize === true,
    text: args.anonymizeText === true,
    logos: args.anonymizeLogos === true,
  };
}

function hasAnonymization(options: AnonymizationOptions) {
  return options.subject || options.text || options.logos;
}

function getAnonymizedTextDescription(options: AnonymizationOptions) {
  if (!options.text) return undefined;
  return "Readable text replaced by numbered lorem placeholder text while preserving color, size, layout, and typography style.";
}

async function uploadBytes(params: {
  bytes: ArrayBuffer;
  contentType: string;
  prefix: string;
  fileName?: string;
}) {
  const url = await uploadBufferToS3({
    buffer: Buffer.from(params.bytes),
    prefix: params.prefix,
    fileName: params.fileName ?? `${Date.now()}`,
    contentType: params.contentType,
  });
  if (!url) throw new ActionError("Failed to upload image");
  return url;
}

async function downloadAndUploadImage(imageUrl: string, fallbackUrl?: string) {
  let response = await fetch(imageUrl);
  if (!response.ok && fallbackUrl) {
    response = await fetch(fallbackUrl);
  }
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new ActionError("Failed to fetch YouTube thumbnail");
  }

  const contentType = response.headers.get("content-type") ?? "image/jpeg";
  return uploadBytes({
    bytes: await response.arrayBuffer(),
    contentType,
    prefix: "inspirations",
    fileName: `thumbnail-${Date.now()}`,
  });
}

function validateImageUpload(args: {
  bytes: ArrayBuffer;
  contentType: string;
  fileName: string;
  maxBytes: number;
}) {
  if (!args.contentType.startsWith("image/")) {
    throw new ActionError("Only images are allowed");
  }
  if (
    args.contentType === "image/svg+xml" ||
    args.contentType === "image/gif" ||
    args.fileName.endsWith(".svg") ||
    args.fileName.endsWith(".gif")
  ) {
    throw new ActionError("SVG and GIF files are not allowed");
  }
  if (args.bytes.byteLength > args.maxBytes) {
    throw new ActionError(
      `File too large (max ${Math.floor(args.maxBytes / 1024 / 1024)}MB)`,
    );
  }
}

export const uploadImage = action({
  args: {
    orgSlug: v.string(),
    bytes: v.bytes(),
    fileName: v.string(),
    contentType: v.string(),
  },
  handler: async (_ctx, args) => {
    validateImageUpload({ ...args, maxBytes: 5 * 1024 * 1024 });
    return uploadBytes({
      bytes: args.bytes,
      contentType: args.contentType,
      prefix: "inspirations",
      fileName: `${Date.now()}-${args.fileName.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, "-")}`,
    });
  },
});

export const uploadPixelatedImage = action({
  args: {
    orgSlug: v.string(),
    imageDataUrl: v.string(),
    originalUrl: v.string(),
  },
  handler: async (_ctx, args) => {
    const matches = args.imageDataUrl.match(/^data:image\/(\w+);base64,(.+)$/);
    if (!matches) throw new ActionError("Invalid image data URL format");

    const [, format, base64Data] = matches;
    const url = await uploadBufferToS3({
      buffer: Buffer.from(base64Data, "base64"),
      prefix: `inspirations/${args.orgSlug}/pixelated`,
      fileName: `${Date.now()}`,
      contentType: `image/${format}`,
    });
    if (!url) throw new ActionError("Failed to upload pixelated image");
    return url;
  },
});

export const create = action({
  args: {
    orgSlug: v.string(),
    type: v.union(v.literal("youtube"), v.literal("upload")),
    youtubeUrl: v.optional(v.string()),
    imageUrls: v.optional(v.array(v.string())),
    anonymize: v.optional(v.boolean()),
    anonymizeSubject: v.optional(v.boolean()),
    anonymizeText: v.optional(v.boolean()),
    anonymizeLogos: v.optional(v.boolean()),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const { org } = await ctx.runQuery(orgContextRef, {
      orgSlug: args.orgSlug,
    });
    const anonymizationOptions = getAnonymizationOptions(args);
    const shouldAnonymize = hasAnonymization(anonymizationOptions);
    const creditCost = shouldAnonymize
      ? CREDIT_COST_PER_ANONYMIZATION
      : CREDIT_COST_PER_INSPIRATION;
    const featureName = shouldAnonymize ? "anonymization" : "inspiration";
    const orgId = org.id;

    const { shouldDeductCredits, encryptedGeminiKey } =
      await validateCreditForFeature(ctx, {
        orgId,
        creditCost,
        featureName,
      });

    let imageUrls: string[];
    let sourceUrl: string | undefined;
    let sourceVideoTitle: string | undefined;
    let sourceVideoAuthor: string | undefined;
    let sourceVideoThumbnailUrl: string | undefined;
    let inspirationName: string | null = null;

    if (args.type === "youtube") {
      if (!args.youtubeUrl) throw new ActionError("YouTube URL is required");
      const videoId = extractVideoId(args.youtubeUrl);
      if (!videoId) throw new ActionError("Invalid YouTube URL");

      imageUrls = [
        await downloadAndUploadImage(
          getThumbnailUrl(videoId),
          getFallbackThumbnailUrl(videoId),
        ),
      ];
      sourceUrl = args.youtubeUrl;

      const videoInfo = await getYoutubeVideoInfo(args.youtubeUrl);
      if (videoInfo) {
        sourceVideoTitle = videoInfo.title;
        sourceVideoAuthor = videoInfo.author ? videoInfo.author : undefined;
        sourceVideoThumbnailUrl = getThumbnailUrl(videoId);
        inspirationName = videoInfo.author
          ? `${videoInfo.title} - ${videoInfo.author}`
type StoredImage = {
  url: string;
  key?: string;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  contentType?: string;
};

type InspirationAccessRow = {
  organizationId: string;
  image?: StoredImage | string | null;
  images?: (StoredImage | string | null)[] | null;
  isPublic?: boolean | null;
  adminReview?: string | null;
  reviewedAt?: number | null;
  deletedAt?: number | null;
};

export const REVIEW_STATUS = {
  GOOD: "GOOD",
  APPROVED: "APPROVED",
  PENDING: "PENDING",
  DENY: "DENY",
} as const;

export type ReviewStatus = (typeof REVIEW_STATUS)[keyof typeof REVIEW_STATUS];

export const publicReviewStatusList = [
  REVIEW_STATUS.GOOD,
  REVIEW_STATUS.APPROVED,
] as const;

const publicReviewStatuses = new Set<ReviewStatus>(publicReviewStatusList);

export const communityReviewRank = {
  [REVIEW_STATUS.GOOD]: 0,
  [REVIEW_STATUS.APPROVED]: 1,
  [REVIEW_STATUS.PENDING]: 2,
  [REVIEW_STATUS.DENY]: 3,
} satisfies Record<ReviewStatus, number>;

export function getReviewStatus(
  inspiration: Pick<
    InspirationAccessRow,
    "adminReview" | "reviewedAt" | "deletedAt"
  >,
): ReviewStatus {
  if (
    inspiration.adminReview === REVIEW_STATUS.GOOD ||
    inspiration.adminReview === REVIEW_STATUS.APPROVED ||
    inspiration.adminReview === REVIEW_STATUS.PENDING ||
    inspiration.adminReview === REVIEW_STATUS.DENY
  ) {
    return inspiration.adminReview;
  }
  if (inspiration.deletedAt) return REVIEW_STATUS.DENY;
  if (inspiration.reviewedAt) return REVIEW_STATUS.APPROVED;
  return REVIEW_STATUS.PENDING;
}

export function canListInCommunity(inspiration: InspirationAccessRow) {
  return (
    !inspiration.deletedAt &&
    inspiration.isPublic !== false &&
    publicReviewStatuses.has(getReviewStatus(inspiration))
  );
}

export function canReadInspiration(
  inspiration: InspirationAccessRow,
  orgId: string,
) {
  if (inspiration.deletedAt) return false;

  return (
    inspiration.organizationId === orgId || canListInCommunity(inspiration)
  );
}

export function getInspirationStoredImages(inspiration: InspirationAccessRow) {
  const images =
    inspiration.images && inspiration.images.length > 0
      ? inspiration.images
      : inspiration.image
        ? [inspiration.image]
        : [];

  return images.flatMap((image): StoredImage[] => {
    if (!image) return [];
    if (typeof image === "string") return [{ url: image }];
    return image.url ? [image] : [];
  });
}

export function toStoredImageUrl(value: StoredImage | string | null) {
  if (!value) return null;
  if (typeof value === "string") return value;
  return value.url;
}

export function getInspirationImageUrls(inspiration: InspirationAccessRow) {
  return getInspirationStoredImages(inspiration)
    .map(toStoredImageUrl)
    .filter((url): url is string => Boolean(url));
}

export function isAnonymizedImageUrl(url: string) {
  return /(?:^|[/?])anonymized-/i.test(url);
}

export function resolveHasPlaceholder(
  hasPlaceholder: boolean | undefined | null,
  thumbnailUrls: string[],
) {
  if (hasPlaceholder) return true;
  return thumbnailUrls.some(isAnonymizedImageUrl);
}

# dev-browser

Browser automation tool that controls browsers through sandboxed JavaScript scripts via CLI.
Scripts run in QuickJS WASM sandbox - not Node.js. No `require`, `fetch`, `fs`, or `process`.

## Setup

If `dev-browser` is not found:
```bash
npm install -g dev-browser
dev-browser install
```

## Core Pattern

Write small, focused scripts. Each script does ONE thing. End by logging state for next decision.

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.goto("https://example.com");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ url: page.url(), title: await page.title() }, null, 2));
EOF
```

## CLI Flags

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--headless` | Launch Chromium in headless mode |
| `--connect [URL]` | Connect to running Chrome/Chromium via CDP (auto-discover Chrome, or use a specific CDP endpoint) |
| `--browser <NAME>` | Select named browser instance (default: "default") |
| `--timeout <SECONDS>` | Max script execution time (default: 30) |

## Browser API

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `browser.getPage(name)` | Get/create named page (persists between scripts) |
| `browser.newPage()` | Create anonymous page (auto-cleanup after script) |
| `browser.listPages()` | List all tabs: `[{id, url, title, name}]` |
| `browser.closePage(name)` | Close named page |

## File I/O (restricted to `~/.dev-browser/tmp/`)

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `await saveScreenshot(buf, name)` | Save screenshot buffer, returns path |
| `await writeFile(name, data)` | Write file, returns path |
| `await readFile(name)` | Read file, returns content |

## Key Workflows

### Discover Unknown Page

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.goto("https://example.com");
const result = await page.snapshotForAI();
console.log(result.full);
EOF
```

Then interact based on discovered elements:
```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }).click();
const result = await page.snapshotForAI({ track: "main" });
console.log(result.full);
EOF
```

### Take Screenshot

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
const buf = await page.screenshot();
const path = await saveScreenshot(buf, "debug.png");
console.log(path);
EOF
```

### Fill Form

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.fill("#email", "user@example.com");
await page.fill("#password", "secret");
await page.click("button[type=submit]");
await page.waitForURL("**/dashboard");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ url: page.url(), title: await page.title() }, null, 2));
EOF
```

### Connect to Running Chrome

```bash
dev-browser --connect <<'EOF'
const tabs = await browser.listPages();
console.log(JSON.stringify(tabs, null, 2));
EOF
```

### Connect to Helium via CDP

Helium is Chromium-based and can be controlled by `dev-browser` when launched with remote debugging enabled. `dev-browser --connect` auto-discovery does not find Helium, so always pass the explicit CDP endpoint.

For a separate automation profile:
```bash
"/Applications/Helium.app/Contents/MacOS/Helium" \
  --remote-debugging-port=9334 \
  --user-data-dir=/tmp/helium-dev-browser-profile \
  --no-first-run \
  --no-default-browser-check
```

Then connect:
```bash
dev-browser --browser helium --connect http://127.0.0.1:9334 <<'EOF'
const tabs = await browser.listPages();
console.log(JSON.stringify(tabs, null, 2));
EOF
```

To automate the user's existing Helium session, Helium must be fully quit and relaunched with `--remote-debugging-port`; an already-running Helium instance that was started without remote debugging cannot be attached by `dev-browser`.

```bash
"/Applications/Helium.app/Contents/MacOS/Helium" --remote-debugging-port=9334
dev-browser --browser helium --connect http://127.0.0.1:9334
```

If Helium is already open without CDP and must not be restarted, use AppleScript or Computer Use for UI-level control instead of `dev-browser`.

### Error Recovery

If a script fails, the page stays where it stopped. Reconnect and inspect:
```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
const path = await saveScreenshot(await page.screenshot(), "debug.png");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ screenshot: path, url: page.url(), title: await page.title() }, null, 2));
EOF
```

## Tips

- Use `page.snapshotForAI()` for structure discovery; use screenshots for visual layout
- Keep page names stable across scripts to resume after failures
- Use `console.log(JSON.stringify(...))` for structured output
- Use `--timeout 10` for scripts that should fail fast
- Pages from `browser.getPage("name")` persist between script runs - no need to re-navigate
- Inside `page.evaluate(...)`, use plain JavaScript only - no TypeScript

## Full API Reference

For complete Playwright Page methods and advanced patterns, see [references/api-reference.md](references/api-reference.md).

**Diagnosing async upload and interaction conflicts**

I'm working through the interplay between asynchronous image uploads and active pointer interactions on the canvas. There’s a tricky race condition where a completed upload during a drag interaction can cause the history state to overwrite the newly added image, due to stale references in interaction data. Preventing this might mean disabling pointer and keyboard input while uploading, even though the user wants to keep editing responsive. I’m considering options like disabling canvas input via a prop during upload to avoid conflicting state updates.

item.text:
**Summarizing UI skill and test results**

I’m preparing to mention how the UI skill influenced the implementation using unprompted material like compact controls and touch properties, keeping the description concise as the user requested. I’ll detail test outcomes clearly: all focused tests passed, the full suite had mostly passes with a couple of known preexisting fails, ESLint passed fully, and TypeScript showed only prior errors. The build compiled all modules successfully, but the final build command exited with an error due to a prerender listener permission issue, so I’ll clarify that the client/server production compilation succeeded despite this. I’ll also note that the runtime port failed to listen due to lacking dev-browser installation, so I’ll mention the skill pause according to rules. Links and bullets will provide clarity without excessive verbosity.
**Noting browser verification and memory citation**

Implemented end-to-end: Thumbfast now has a custom, fullscreen drawing inspiration editor with no Excalidraw.

- [Drawing editor](/Users/melvynx/Developer/experiments/benchmarks/benchmarks/thumbfast/2026-07-15-codex-gpt-5-6-sol-2/src/features/drawing/drawing-editor.tsx:46): selection, move/resize, text editing, shapes, arrows, pencil, images, person placeholders, shortcuts, undo/redo, templates, and unsaved-navigation protection.
- [Document model and templates](/Users/melvynx/Developer/experiments/benchmarks/benchmarks/thumbfast/2026-07-15-codex-gpt-5-6-sol-2/src/features/drawing/drawing-document.ts:132): typed, validated, serializable editable scenes.
- [Save/reopen flow](/Users/melvynx/Developer/experiments/benchmarks/benchmarks/thumbfast/2026-07-15-codex-gpt-5-6-sol-2/src/features/drawing/drawing-inspiration-page.tsx:32): durable PNG preview plus structured drawing data.
- [Convex integration](/Users/melvynx/Developer/experiments/benchmarks/benchmarks/thumbfast/2026-07-15-codex-gpt-5-6-sol-2/convex/inspiration.ts:478): organization authorization, plan limits, create/update/load, normal list/detail/selector and generation-image integration.
- Port defaults are consistently `9155`; browser and visible titles are exactly `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- The interface-quality pass produced compact 40px controls, touch-accessible properties, restrained shadows, and clear selection feedback.

Verification:

- Full ESLint: passed.
- Focused feature tests: 18/18 passed.
- Full suite: 198 passed, 3 skipped; two unrelated existing sign-in tests still expect “Sign in” while the UI says “Send code”.
- Typecheck: only the existing Streamdown/Shiki incompatibility at `message.tsx:333`.
- Client/server production compilation completed across 5,908 modules. Final prerender and live browser verification were blocked because this sandbox rejects local listeners with `EPERM`; the required `dev-browser` CLI is also unavailable.
